slides.headline: October 10, 2014: India got its first Nobel Peace Prize - shared with a 17-year-old from Pakistan.
The Norwegian Nobel Committee named Kailash Satyarthi and Malala Yousafzai joint winners of the 2014 Nobel Peace Prize
slides.body: Satyarthi, founder of Bachpan Bachao Andolan, had spent decades fighting child labour and campaigning for every child's right to education. The prize recognized him as the first Indian-born person ever to win it.

slides.headline: An Indian Hindu man and a Pakistani Muslim teenager, honored together, for the same cause.
slides.body: The Nobel Committee deliberately paired an Indian and a Pakistani laureate for their shared struggle against the suppression of children and for universal education - a message as pointed as the prize itself.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat measures itself by how it treats its most powerless citizens, not just its most powerful institutions.
slides.body: Satyarthi's prize wasn't for an invention or an institution - it was for decades spent insisting that childhood itself shouldn't be optional.
